name: Protected User Data
description:
Adversaries may utilize standard operating system APIs to collect data from permission-backed data stores on a device, such as the calendar or contact list. These permissions need to be declared ahead of time. On Android, they must be included in the application’s manifest. On iOS, they must be included in the application’s `Info.plist` file.  

 

In almost all cases, the user is required to grant access to the data store that the application is trying to access. In recent OS versions, vendors have introduced additional privacy controls for users, such as the ability to grant permission to an application only while the application is being actively used by the user. 

 

If the device has been jailbroken or rooted, an adversary may be able to access [Protected User Data](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1636) without the user’s knowledge or approval.

telemetry.name: API Calls
telemetry.description: Instrumented mobile API calls and results relevant to an application behavior.
telemetry.collection_focus: Instrument selected APIs in the owned test app or approved research build; log caller, API, sanitized argument class and return status.

providers.name: Android logcat
providers.scope: Permitted logs from a consented test device/emulator; output depends on build, permissions and instrumentation.

providers.name: Android dumpsys
providers.scope: Point-in-time service/package state on an authorized development device.

providers.name: Instrumented test application
providers.scope: Own-app permission, API and state callbacks; not universal visibility into other apps.

configuration: Use a disposable emulator or owned development device with approved debugging. Record OS/API level, app version and instrumentation privileges.
Collect only relevant logcat buffers/tags and service snapshots; add explicit own-app instrumentation for events absent from OS logs.
Forward sanitized logs and compare before/after state. Remove test data and revoke debugging access after the lab session.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Android tooling does not imply iOS coverage. Standard mobile apps cannot observe all other apps or protected OS internals; MDM status is not full API, filesystem or content telemetry.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per owned device, app version and permission state: unexpected API/permission changes, background activity and network destinations. OS privacy restrictions and emulator differences limit observability.

telemetry.name: Network Traffic Flow
telemetry.description: Connection/flow summaries such as endpoints, duration, byte counts and transport.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect Zeek conn.log, Suricata flow events or exporter equivalents, including observation point and sampling settings.

providers.name: Zeek
providers.scope: Connection and protocol metadata from traffic visible to the sensor.

providers.name: Suricata EVE
providers.scope: Configured flow, alert, DNS, HTTP, TLS and protocol records.

providers.name: AWS VPC Flow Logs
providers.scope: IP traffic metadata alternative; no packet payload or DNS answer history, and some traffic is not logged.

configuration: Use an authorized lab TAP/SPAN, virtual mirror or gateway interface. Define which traffic crosses it; avoid assuming visibility into every segment.
Enable the required Zeek analyzers or Suricata EVE event types. Export logs with sensor identity, clock synchronization and flow correlation identifiers.
Monitor capture loss, truncation and exporter sampling. Capture payload only with approval and restrictive retention; encryption normally prevents plaintext inspection.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Flows are not packet payloads. NAT, asymmetric routes, encryption, missing mirrors and sampling can hide attribution or content. A destination connection alone does not prove malicious intent.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per source and observation point: connection rate, destination-host/port fan-out, response/failure ratio and previously unseen destinations. Compare equivalent time windows; separate authorized scanners, NAT and sampling effects.

telemetry.name: Permissions Request
telemetry.description: A system prompt for an application permission, with request and response context where observable.
telemetry.collection_focus: Correlate own-app request/callback instrumentation with the consented test-device prompt. A request callback alone does not prove a prompt appeared (for example, a previously denied permission).

analytics.name: Analytic 1786
analytics.guidance: For Android, detect Protected User Data by correlating analyst-visible device/network evidence and management state; use streaming or batched telemetry only where the documented collector is deployed. Correlate API Calls via Application Vetting / Instrumented Dynamic Analysis [Dynamic API/runtime trace: ContentResolver.query() to sensitive provider URI (contacts, calendar, call_log, sms) with query_count > $ContentQueryThreshold$ by app NOT IN $ApprovedDataApps$]; Network Traffic Flow via Android Enterprise Network Logging / Enterprise VPN [DevicePolicyManager.retrieveNetworkLogs(): DnsEvent / ConnectEvent; VPN flow metadata]; Permissions Request via Android Enterprise DPC / Application Vetting [DevicePolicyManager.getPermissionGrantState(); PackageManager manifest/requested-permission review]. Alert on a sequence or state change inconsistent with the device/app baseline, approved management policy, or expected user workflow; do not infer unobserved API calls, file/process activity, or payload content from management state alone.

tuning.description: Per-data-type approved apps: calendar sync, dialer, SMS default, CRM apps. Derive from MDM catalog.
Varies by data type: Contacts=50, Calendar=30, CallLog=10, SMS=20 queries/2min. Derive from per-app baseline.
Default 100KB. Adjust per data-type expected size.

log_sources.name: mobile:DynamicAnalysis
log_sources.channel: Dynamic API/runtime trace: ContentResolver.query() to sensitive provider URI (contacts, calendar, call_log, sms) with query_count > $ContentQueryThreshold$ by app NOT IN $ApprovedDataApps$

analytics.name: Analytic 1787
analytics.guidance: For iOS, detect Protected User Data by correlating analyst-visible device/network evidence and management state; use streaming or batched telemetry only where the documented collector is deployed. Correlate API Calls via Application Vetting / Instrumented Dynamic Analysis [Dynamic API/runtime trace: CNContactStore.enumerateContacts or EKEventStore.fetchEvents or CLLocationManager.startUpdatingLocation called with broad scope by app NOT IN $ApprovedDataApps$]; Network Traffic Flow via Apple Network Extension / Enterprise VPN [NEFilterFlow / per-app VPN / secure-web-gateway flow metadata]; Permissions Request via Application Vetting [Code-signing entitlements and Info.plist privacy usage-description keys]. Alert on a sequence or state change inconsistent with the device/app baseline, approved management policy, or expected user workflow; do not infer unobserved API calls, file/process activity, or payload content from management state alone.

mitigations.name: Use Recent OS Version
mitigations.description: OS feature updates often enhance security and privacy around permissions.

mitigations.name: User Guidance
mitigations.description: Users should be taught the danger behind granting unnecessary permissions to an application and should be advised to use extra scrutiny when an application requests them.

simulation.prerequisites: Use owned test devices or emulators, disposable app accounts and test data. Verify platform/version instrumentation; desktop test procedures do not establish mobile coverage.

synthetic.purpose: Collection/parser contract exercise, NOT a positive example or detection of this TTP.
